editor_note: No semantic drift: the shots precedence list, the twirling admonition ("le job échoue si `twirling` est activé et que le produit de `num_randomizations` et `shots_per_randomization` est inférieur à la valeur de `shots`") and every default/choice value match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is four terminology renderings in the options/compatibility tables: `environment.job_tags` "List of tags" → "Liste de balises" ("balises" reads as markup tags; French uses "tags"/"étiquettes"), "basis gate names to unroll to" → "portes de base à déplier" (calque of "unroll"; the sense is decomposition — "vers lesquelles décomposer"), the incompatibility bullet "Stretches" translated to "Étirements" (an OpenQASM `stretch` feature name that should stay English, otherwise the reader cannot map it to anything), and "non-Clifford entanglers" → "enchevêtreurs non-Clifford" (the conventional French root for entanglement is "intrication", so "portes d'intrication non-Clifford"). None of these teach a false concept, and "Liste d'interactions à deux qubits dirigées" is merely awkward adjective placement.

examples.source: List of tags.
examples.suggested: Liste de tags.
examples.translation: Liste de balises.
examples.why: For `environment.job_tags`, "balises" is the French word for markup/HTML tags or beacons; job tags are labels attached to a job. French Qiskit users say "tags" or "étiquettes".

examples.source: List of basis gate names to unroll to
examples.suggested: Liste des noms de portes de base vers lesquelles décomposer le circuit
examples.translation: Liste des noms de portes de base à déplier
examples.why: "Déplier" is a literal calque of "unroll"; the operation described is decomposing the circuit into that basis, and the French as written suggests unfolding the gates themselves.

examples.source: - Stretches
examples.suggested: - Stretches
examples.translation: - Étirements
examples.why: "Stretches" here is the OpenQASM `stretch` duration feature name, listed as incompatible with gate twirling; translated to "Étirements" it becomes unidentifiable, since no French doc or API surface uses that word.

examples.source: Does not work with non-Clifford entanglers.
examples.suggested: Ne fonctionne pas avec les portes d'intrication non-Clifford.
examples.translation: Ne fonctionne pas avec les enchevêtreurs non-Clifford.
examples.why: The conventional French term for entanglement in quantum computing is "intrication"; "enchevêtreur" is a non-standard coinage that a French-speaking quantum engineer would not write.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — I checked every quantitative and conditional claim (syndrome « 11 » → bloc du milieu, « quatre portes CNOT de moins », « au plus un bloc en subisse un nombre impair », « pire qu'aucun code lorsque p est supérieur à un demi », point d'équilibre 0,0323, la non-commutation XZ = -ZX) and found no drift, no inverted condition, no hallucinated sentence, including in the final probability/break-even section. Terminology is correct and consistent (code interne/code externe, erreurs de retournement de bit/de phase, mesure du syndrome, dégénérescence, qubit logique/qubits physiques), and the nous/on register holds with no vous/veuillez slips. What a native technical editor would change is a handful of calques: « le code interne semble en quelque sorte "être dans le chemin" » (anglicism for "in the way"; French would say « faire obstacle »/« gêner »), « Cela peut être raisonné en utilisant les relations… » (raisonner is not transitive that way; « On peut le justifier à l'aide de… »), « vérifier ces trois qubits du code externe pour les erreurs Z » (calqued "check X for Y"), and « c'est tricher le modèle de bruit » (tricher requires avec/sur). Also « Trois virgule vingt-cinq pour cent environ » spells out a decimal in a way no French technical writer would (« Environ 3,25 % »), and line 114's « au plus une erreur X ou au plus une erreur Z peuvent être détectées » should take a singular verb. None of these mislead the learner.

examples.source: but the inner code seems to be somehow "in the way," making the detection and correction of these errors slightly more difficult.
examples.suggested: mais le code interne semble en quelque sorte « faire obstacle », ce qui rend la détection et la correction de ces erreurs un peu plus difficiles.
examples.translation: mais le code interne semble en quelque sorte « être dans le chemin », rendant la détection et la correction de ces erreurs légèrement plus difficile.
examples.why: « être dans le chemin » is a direct calque of the English idiom; standard French uses « faire obstacle » / « gêner ». Also « plus difficile » should agree with the coordinated plural subject (« plus difficiles »).

examples.source: This can be reasoned using the relationships between $Z$ and CNOT gates described above
examples.suggested: On peut le justifier à l'aide des relations entre portes $Z$ et CNOT décrites ci-dessus
examples.translation: Cela peut être raisonné en utilisant les relations entre les portes $Z$ et CNOT décrites ci-dessus
examples.why: « raisonner » is not used transitively in French; « Cela peut être raisonné » reads as raw MT. A French author writes « On peut le justifier / s'en convaincre à l'aide de… ».

examples.source: but that's cheating the noise model
examples.suggested: mais c'est tricher avec le modèle de bruit
examples.translation: mais c'est tricher le modèle de bruit
examples.why: « tricher » is intransitive and requires a preposition (tricher avec/sur). As written it is ungrammatical and reads as a word-for-word carry-over of the English.

examples.source: Three and a quarter percent or so may not seem like a very good break-even point
examples.suggested: Environ 3,25 % peut sembler un point d'équilibre assez médiocre
examples.translation: Trois virgule vingt-cinq pour cent environ peut ne pas sembler un très bon point d'équilibre
examples.why: Spelling out a decimal figure (« Trois virgule vingt-cinq pour cent ») is not done in French technical prose; the numeral form « 3,25 % » is the convention, and fronting « Environ » avoids the heavy subject.

examples.source: We can then check these three qubits of the outer code for $Z$ errors
examples.suggested: On peut ensuite rechercher d'éventuelles erreurs $Z$ sur ces trois qubits du code externe
examples.translation: On peut ensuite vérifier ces trois qubits du code externe pour les erreurs $Z$
examples.why: « vérifier X pour Y » is a calque of the English "check X for Y"; French inverts the construction with « rechercher / détecter d'éventuelles erreurs sur… ».

editor_note: No semantic drift and no hallucination: PUB value counts (au maximum quatre/trois valeurs), the commuting-observables caveat, the NumPy broadcasting rules, all four example shapes and the BitArray axis description (gauche = shots, droite = bytes) all match the English exactly, and domain terms are correct and consistent (expectation value → valeur d'espérance, standard deviations → écarts-types, shots/broadcasting kept in English as the field does). The only editorial defects are stiffness calques in the "Broadcasting rules" example list: dimensions are written "un tableau de 5x1 / de 1x6 / de 4x6" where a French technical writer writes "un tableau 5×1" (or "de taille 5×1"), repeated across all four examples; and "possède un ensemble de valeurs de paramètres" is a literal rendering of "has a …" where "comporte" or a simple "avec" would read natively. Neither could mislead a learner — both are surface phrasing.

examples.source: has a parameter value set that is a 5x1 array and a 1x1 observables array
examples.suggested: porte sur un ensemble de valeurs de paramètres sous forme de tableau 5×1 et un tableau d'observables 1×1
examples.translation: possède un ensemble de valeurs de paramètres qui est un tableau de 5x1 et un tableau d'observables de 1x1
examples.why: "un tableau de 5x1" is a calque of the English apposition; French technical writing puts the dimensions directly after the noun ("un tableau 5×1") or spells out "de taille 5×1". The pattern repeats in all four examples (5x1, 1x6, 4x1, 4x6, 3x6, 3x1), so it reads as machine-produced rather than authored.

examples.source: Example 1: (broadcast single observable) has a parameter value set …
examples.suggested: Exemple 1 : (broadcast d'un seul observable) comporte un ensemble de valeurs de paramètres …
examples.translation: Exemple 1 : (broadcast d'un seul observable) possède un ensemble de valeurs de paramètres …
examples.why: "posséder" for the English inanimate "to have" is stiff in French; "comporte" / "utilise" is what a native technical writer would use. Used identically in Examples 1-3.

examples.source: As a first example, let us look at the following ten-qubit circuit:
examples.suggested: Commençons par un premier exemple : le circuit suivant à dix qubits.
examples.translation: Comme premier exemple, examinons le circuit suivant à dix qubits :
examples.why: "Comme premier exemple" is a word-for-word transposition of "As a first example"; French prefers "Pour un premier exemple" or a "Commençons par…" construction. Understandable, purely stylistic.

editor_note: No misleading content: all load-bearing numbers and claims survive intact (156 qubits Heron r3, 10 minutes de temps QPU par mois, 200 à 300 µs de temps de cohérence, profondeurs transpilées à deux qubits de 80 ou plus, profondeur du circuit = 9), the tu-register holds throughout, and core terms are correct (qubit, intrication, portes d'intrication, fidélité de couche, largeur du circuit, transpilation, valeur d'espérance, un observable). What a native technical editor would change: "prime factorization" is rendered throughout the worked example as "factorisation première" (l.193, 198, 199, 203), a calque — standard French is "factorisation en nombres premiers" / "décomposition en facteurs premiers". There is an outright grammar slip at l.313, "indiquer au gestionnaire de ressources quelles ressources nous avons besoin" (avoir besoin DE → "de quelles ressources nous avons besoin"), plus a within-file split on single-qubit gates ("portes à qubit unique" l.88 vs "portes à un qubit" l.166), the calque "scientifiques computationnels" (l.130), a small directional slip in the storage paragraph, and an infinitive instruction ("déduire", l.63) that breaks the tu-imperative used in the other exercises.

examples.source: Estimate how much CPU time and memory the prime factorization might require. / the scheduler assigns CPU cores and memory to the prime factorization task
examples.suggested: …que la factorisation en nombres premiers pourrait nécessiter / …à la tâche de décomposition en facteurs premiers
examples.translation: Estimer le temps CPU et la mémoire que la factorisation première pourrait nécessiter. / l'ordonnanceur assigne des cœurs CPU et de la mémoire à la tâche de factorisation première
examples.why: "Factorisation première" is a word-for-word calque of "prime factorization"; the established French mathematical terms are "factorisation en nombres premiers" or "décomposition en facteurs premiers". Recognizable, so not misleading, but no French mathematician writes it this way — and it recurs four times.

examples.source: Now we need to tell the resource manager what resources we need to execute this program.
examples.suggested: Nous devons maintenant indiquer au gestionnaire de ressources de quelles ressources nous avons besoin pour exécuter ce programme.
examples.translation: Nous devons maintenant indiquer au gestionnaire de ressources quelles ressources nous avons besoin pour exécuter ce programme.
examples.why: Grammatical error: "avoir besoin" governs "de", so the interrogative must be "de quelles ressources". As written it is the English relative-clause pattern transplanted into French — a native technical writer would not produce this.

examples.source: multiple single-qubit gates to be executed on a qubit in sequence … two-qubit gates have much higher error rates than single-qubit gates
examples.suggested: Use "portes à un qubit" in both places (matching "portes à deux qubits").
examples.translation: plusieurs portes à qubit unique en séquence sur un même qubit … les portes à deux qubits ont des taux d'erreur bien plus élevés que les portes à un qubit
examples.why: The same concept is rendered two ways within one file. "Portes à un qubit" (used later) is the conventional form and pairs symmetrically with "portes à deux qubits"; "portes à qubit unique" is a one-off calque. The concept stays identifiable, so MINOR.

examples.source: parallel file systems, shared network storage, and object-based systems enable rapid access across many compute nodes
examples.suggested: …permettent un accès rapide depuis de nombreux nœuds de calcul (ou : un accès rapide partagé entre de nombreux nœuds de calcul)
examples.translation: les systèmes de fichiers parallèles, le stockage réseau partagé et les systèmes à objets permettent un accès rapide à de nombreux nœuds de calcul
examples.why: "Across many compute nodes" means the storage is reachable FROM many nodes; "un accès rapide À de nombreux nœuds" reverses the relationship, making the nodes the thing being accessed. Low-impact in context, but it flips the direction of the sentence.

examples.source: Use the descriptions above to infer some advantages and disadvantages of the different scaling approaches (vertical and horizontal).
examples.suggested: À partir des descriptions ci-dessus, déduis quelques avantages et inconvénients…
examples.translation: À partir des descriptions ci-dessus, déduire quelques avantages et inconvénients des deux approches de mise à l'échelle : verticale et horizontale.
examples.why: The file otherwise addresses the learner with "tu" and second-person imperatives ("Vérifie ta compréhension", "Suppose que tu essaies…", "indique à quelle étape…"). The bare infinitive here reads as an impersonal exercise rubric and breaks the pedagogical voice.

examples.source: exposed to computational scientists in the form of programming abstractions
examples.suggested: exposées aux chercheurs en calcul scientifique sous la forme d'abstractions de programmation
examples.translation: exposées aux scientifiques computationnels sous la forme d'abstractions de programmation
examples.why: "Scientifiques computationnels" is a direct calque; French uses "chercheurs/scientifiques en calcul scientifique" or "numériciens". Understandable but not idiomatic.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: I checked every prose paragraph against the source (Pauli-Lindblad model description, LayerError/rates/generators paragraph, the three EstimatorV2 option-passing routes, the "three boxes, two of which contain InjectNoise annotations with different ref attributes (since they are not equivalent)" passage, and the ref/modifier_ref bullets) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or invented claim; domain terms are correct and consistent ("couche d'intrication", "portes d'intrication", "taux d'erreur", "gestionnaire de passes", "twirling" kept in English, "job"/"primitive" kept). What a native technical editor would still change is a handful of English-shaped constructions. The worst is "Similaire aux primitives, tu peux spécifier les options…" (line ~338), where the adjective dangles onto "tu" — French requires "Comme pour les primitives, tu peux…"; the same calque appears more forgivably at line ~237 ("Similaire à `NoiseLearner`, la classe…", where "À l'instar de" would be idiomatic). Line ~231 has a dangling participle plus an ambiguous pronoun ("Après avoir passé le modèle de bruit à l'objet `EstimatorV2`, il peut être utilisé…" — "il" could be the model or the object), and "un `BoxOp` annoté par twirling" reads as a process rather than what the source means (a BoxOp carrying a `Twirl` annotation). Finally the register slips in the Next-steps list: the body uses tu-imperatives ("Consulte la documentation API") but the bullets switch to infinitives ("Consulter la référence API", "Apprendre à implémenter").

examples.source: Similar to the primitives, you can specify the options during or after instantiating the `NoiseLearnerV3` object.
examples.suggested: Comme pour les primitives, tu peux spécifier les options au moment de l'instanciation de l'objet `NoiseLearnerV3` ou après.
examples.translation: Similaire aux primitives, tu peux spécifier les options lors de l'instanciation ou après avoir instancié l'objet `NoiseLearnerV3`.
examples.why: Direct calque of the English absolute phrase: in French the adjective "Similaire" has to agree with a following subject, and here that subject is "tu", so the sentence is ungrammatical. A native writer uses "Comme pour…" / "À l'instar des primitives…".

examples.source: After the noise model is passed into the `EstimatorV2` object, it can be used to run workloads and perform error mitigation as normal.
examples.suggested: Une fois le modèle de bruit passé à l'objet `EstimatorV2`, celui-ci peut être utilisé pour exécuter des charges de travail et effectuer l'atténuation d'erreurs comme d'habitude.
examples.translation: Après avoir passé le modèle de bruit à l'objet `EstimatorV2`, il peut être utilisé pour exécuter des charges de travail et effectuer l'atténuation d'erreurs normalement.
examples.why: The participle "avoir passé" has no subject matching "il", and "il" is ambiguous between the model and the object; the English is unambiguous (the EstimatorV2 object is what gets used). Meaning is recoverable, so MINOR, but a French editor would rewrite it.

examples.source: each of which must be a twirled-annotated [`BoxOp`](…) containing [ISA](…) operations
examples.suggested: dont chacune doit être un `BoxOp` portant une annotation `Twirl` et contenant des opérations ISA
examples.translation: dont chacune doit être un [`BoxOp`](…) annoté par twirling contenant des opérations [ISA](…)
examples.why: "annoté par twirling" suggests the box was annotated by means of twirling, whereas the source means it carries the `Twirl` annotation shown in the output below (Twirl(group='pauli', …)). Recognizable, not false, hence MINOR.

examples.source: Refer to the … API documentation … / Review the [EstimatorOptions API reference] …
examples.suggested: Keep the tu-imperative in the bullets: "Consulte la référence API EstimatorOptions…", "Apprends à implémenter…"
examples.translation: Consulte la documentation API … / - Consulter la [référence API EstimatorOptions] … - Apprendre à implémenter …
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency in imperative style: body prose uses the informal tu-imperative, the Next-steps bullets switch to bare infinitives. Not misleading, but the file should pick one convention.

examples.source: The job result is a list of `NoiseLearnerV3Result` objects, one for each input-boxed set of instructions.
examples.suggested: …, un par ensemble d'instructions encadré (boxed) fourni en entrée.
examples.translation: Le résultat du job est une liste d'objets `NoiseLearnerV3Result`, un pour chaque ensemble d'instructions en boîte en entrée.
examples.why: "en boîte en entrée" stacks two "en" phrases and reads as machine output; the sense is right but the phrasing is stiff.

editor_note: Pure bibliography: the only prose is the title/description/headings, and all are idiomatic and faithful ("Works cited" → "Références citées", "Full list of references" → "Liste complète des références", description → "Ce document fournit la liste complète de toutes les citations utilisées dans le cours."); the 136 numbered citations [1]–[136] are correctly left verbatim in English with identical authors, venues, page ranges, dates and DOIs (spot-checked [39] Gidney/Ekerå "8 hours … 20 million noisy qubits", [40] "177 Days with 13 436 Qubits", [95] Ajtai NP-hard SVP), so there is no drift, no dropped or invented reference, and nothing a native editor would change.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the garbled English sentence at "provides a DataBin ... objects should be used" is sensibly rendered as "l'SDK Qiskit mette a disposizione gli oggetti ...", and informal register holds ("Per ulteriori informazioni consulta la documentazione API"). Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) The loanword "primitive" is treated as a masculine noun with mismatched agreement — "le interfacce dei primitive Qiskit", "del primitive Estimator", "del primitive Sampler"; Italian Qiskit usage is feminine ("le primitive", "della primitiva Estimator") or, if kept in English, needs a head noun ("della primitiva Estimator"). It is at least self-consistent, so the concept stays identifiable. (2) In the execution section the English hedge "these interfaces should be able to provide" is hardened to "queste interfacce devono fornire", while the parallel "should, at minimum, contain a Target" was correctly kept conditional ("dovrebbe contenere almeno un Target") — an inconsistent modality that turns a recommendation into a requirement. Minor secondary note: "un QPU" (masc.) is used throughout where Italian docs usually write "una QPU"; defensible if read as "processore", so not counted.

examples.source: Exposing that capability can be done by creating implementations of the Qiskit primitives interfaces
examples.suggested: È possibile esporre questa capacità creando implementazioni delle interfacce delle primitive di Qiskit
examples.translation: È possibile esporre questa capacità creando implementazioni delle interfacce dei primitive Qiskit
examples.why: "dei primitive" mismatches article and number with the invariant English loanword; Italian Qiskit convention is feminine "le primitive" (or "la primitiva Estimator"). Same pattern recurs in "del primitive Estimator" and "del primitive Sampler" — consistent, so not misleading, but visibly non-native.

examples.source: At minimum, these interfaces should be able to provide a method for execution, querying job status, and returning the job results.
examples.suggested: Come minimo, queste interfacce dovrebbero fornire un metodo per l'esecuzione, la verifica dello stato del job e la restituzione dei risultati del job.
examples.translation: Come minimo, queste interfacce devono fornire un metodo per l'esecuzione, la verifica dello stato del job e la restituzione dei risultati del job.
examples.why: "should be able to provide" is a recommendation; "devono fornire" states an obligation. The file already renders the parallel "should, at minimum, contain a Target" as "dovrebbe contenere almeno un Target", so the modality is inconsistent within the page.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, quantifier and caveat matches the English, including the delicate ones ("se e solo se gli elementi fuori diagonale erano già tutti nulli", "definito solo quando la probabilità p(a) è non nulla", the three-way equivalence of Tr(P_a ρ_X) and the conditional-state summary at the end). Core terminology is correct and consistent throughout: misura/misura proiettiva, matrici semidefinite positive, matrici densità, matrici di Kraus, rappresentazione di Choi, sfera di Bloch, stato classico-quantistico. What a native technical editor would still change is stylistic: the false friend "consistente con" (used twice, lines 374 and 555) where Italian technical prose wants "coerente con"; the calque "Tracciando fuori il sistema di output Y" (line 434) for "tracing out", where Italian physics says "tracciando via"/"prendendo la traccia parziale su"; the calque "che sommano alla matrice identità" (line 34) and "questo è effettivamente il caso" (line 100); and the slightly ambiguous "i cui autovalori sono tutti 0 oppure 1" (line 82), which can momentarily read as "all 0, or all 1" instead of the English "all either 0 or 1". None of these mislead; the informal-tu convention holds ("Prova a dimostrarlo prima per prodotti tensoriali...").

examples.source: This expression is consistent with our description of general measurements in terms of matrices
examples.suggested: Questa espressione è coerente con la nostra descrizione delle misure generali in termini di matrici
examples.translation: Questa espressione è consistente con la nostra descrizione delle misure generali in termini di matrici
examples.why: 'consistente' is a false friend in Italian (it means 'substantial/solid'); the logical sense of English 'consistent' is 'coerente'. Recurs at line 555 ('le probabilità degli esiti sono consistenti con le nostre osservazioni precedenti').

examples.source: Tracing out the output system Y (which is the system on the right) yields
examples.suggested: Tracciando via il sistema di output Y (che è il sistema a destra) si ottiene / Prendendo la traccia parziale sul sistema di output Y...
examples.translation: Tracciando fuori il sistema di output Y (che è il sistema a destra) si ottiene
examples.why: 'tracciando fuori' is a literal calque of 'tracing out'; Italian quantum-information prose uses 'tracciare via' or an explicit 'traccia parziale su', which is also the term the course itself uses elsewhere (operatorname{Tr}_X = traccia parziale).

examples.source: a collection of projection matrices that sum to the identity matrix / The following two observations establish that this is the case.
examples.suggested: una collezione di matrici di proiezione la cui somma è la matrice identità / Le due osservazioni seguenti stabiliscono che è proprio così.
examples.translation: una collezione di matrici di proiezione che sommano alla matrice identità / Le seguenti due osservazioni mostrano che questo è effettivamente il caso.
examples.why: Both are English syntax carried over: Italian normally nominalizes ('la cui somma è...') rather than using 'sommare a' intransitively, and 'questo è il caso' is a calque of 'this is the case'. Grammatical but stiff for a native technical writer.

examples.source: they can alternatively be defined as positive semidefinite matrices whose eigenvalues are all either 0 or 1
examples.suggested: ...matrici semidefinite positive i cui autovalori valgono ciascuno 0 oppure 1
examples.translation: possono essere definite alternativamente come matrici semidefinite positive i cui autovalori sono tutti 0 oppure 1
examples.why: 'tutti 0 oppure 1' can be parsed as 'all equal to 0, or all equal to 1', losing the English 'each one is either 0 or 1'. The surrounding context repairs it, so it does not mislead, but the distributive reading should be made explicit in teaching material.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere: every FAQ answer matches its English counterpart, including the tricky negations ("Non ti verranno addebitati costi a meno che tu non crei un'istanza Pay-As-You-Go", "Un bearer token non può essere usato per autenticarsi al servizio Qiskit Runtime") and the odd-but-faithful "puoi vedere e usare solo le istanze create nell'istanza a cui hai effettuato l'accesso". Informal "tu" holds throughout (Cita, Prova, consulta, devi, vuoi). What a native technical editor would still change: academic "acknowledge IBM Quantum" is rendered as "ringraziare IBM Quantum" (= thank), which clashes with the quoted blockquote right below it that correctly says "Riconosciamo l'utilizzo dei servizi IBM Quantum"; "[computer software]" is calqued as "[software per computer]" instead of the conventional "[software]"/"[programma per computer]"; "workload" is rendered "carichi di lavoro" in the billing FAQ but left as English "workload" in the device-drift FAQ; and the metapackage paragraph mixes passato remoto "furono combinati" with passato prossimo "è stata rimossa" in adjacent sentences.

examples.source: we encourage authors to acknowledge IBM Quantum® by using:
examples.suggested: incoraggiamo gli autori a riconoscere l'uso di IBM Quantum® utilizzando:
examples.translation: incoraggiamo gli autori a ringraziare IBM Quantum® usando:
examples.why: In academic usage "acknowledge" is "riconoscere / inserire nei ringraziamenti", not "ringraziare" (to thank). The blockquote immediately following already uses "Riconosciamo", so the lead-in contradicts its own quoted text.

examples.source: Estimator primitive (Version x.y.z) [computer software]
examples.suggested: Estimator primitive (Versione x.y.z) [software]
examples.translation: Estimator primitive (Versione x.y.z) [software per computer]
examples.why: "software per computer" is a word-for-word calque of the English citation-format bracket; Italian bibliographic style uses simply [software] or [programma per computer].

examples.source: use it to send workloads to QPUs / If a particular workload is very sensitive
examples.suggested: pick one rendering (either "carico di lavoro" or English "workload") and use it in both places
examples.translation: la utilizzi per inviare carichi di lavoro alle QPU / Se un determinato workload è molto sensibile
examples.why: The same domain term is rendered two different ways within the file; harmless for comprehension but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: These separate software packages were combined into what was called the Qiskit metapackage ... This metapackage architecture was removed with the release of the Qiskit SDK v1.0
examples.suggested: Questi pacchetti software separati sono stati combinati in quello che veniva chiamato il *metapacchetto* Qiskit ...
examples.translation: Questi pacchetti software separati furono combinati in quello che veniva chiamato il *metapacchetto* Qiskit ... Questa architettura a metapacchetto è stata rimossa con la release di Qiskit SDK v1.0
examples.why: Passato remoto ("furono combinati") next to passato prossimo ("è stata rimossa") for events of the same recent period reads inconsistently; technical documentation in Italian stays with passato prossimo.

editor_note: Nothing here misleads: the whole conceptual chain (oracolo/scatola nera, promessa e input "don't care", gate a query unitari, matrice di permutazione, norma euclidea) is faithful, complete and pedagogically as clear as the English, and the informal "noi" register holds throughout. Four editorial slips remain. (1) The visible DefinitionTooltip body for "accesso casuale" is left entirely in English ("Random access, also known as direct access, refers to…"), so the learner who opens the tooltip gets untranslated prose. (2) "entries" of a matrix/vector is rendered "voci" twice ("tutte le altre voci pari a 0", "mescola le voci del vettore") — a calque; Italian linear algebra says "elementi"/"componenti". (3) "la funzione di input $f$ viene acceduta tramite questi gate" is an English passive calque; "accedere" is intransitive in Italian, so a native would write "si accede alla funzione di input $f$ tramite questi gate". (4) "we sometimes come up with very complicated and highly contrived problems" becomes "a volte ci imbattiamo in problemi… artificiosi", turning deliberate construction into stumbling upon them; plus the heading "## gate a query" is uncapitalized where every other heading is sentence-capitalized.

examples.source: with all other entries being $0.$ … simply shuffles the entries of the vector
examples.suggested: con tutti gli altri elementi pari a $0.$ … semplicemente permuta gli elementi del vettore
examples.translation: con tutte le altre voci pari a $0.$ … semplicemente mescola le voci del vettore
examples.why: "voci" is a calque of "entries" (voce = dictionary/list entry). The standard Italian term for matrix/vector entries is "elementi" (or "componenti"). Recognizable, but not the domain convention.

examples.source: the input function $f$ is accessed through these gates
examples.suggested: si accede alla funzione di input $f$ tramite questi gate
examples.translation: la funzione di input $f$ viene acceduta tramite questi gate
examples.why: "venire acceduto" is a direct calque of the English passive; "accedere" is intransitive in Italian and takes "a", so the passive is ungrammatical-sounding to a native technical writer.

examples.source: we sometimes come up with very complicated and highly contrived problems
examples.suggested: a volte costruiamo (o ideiamo) problemi molto complessi e altamente artificiosi
examples.translation: a volte ci imbattiamo in problemi molto complessi e altamente artificiosi
examples.why: "ci imbattiamo in" = "we stumble upon". The English point is that researchers deliberately invent these contrived problems; the Italian makes them something met by chance, weakening the follow-up that contrived problems are still worth studying.

examples.source: <DefinitionTooltip definition="Random access, also known as direct access, refers to the ability to look at elements at chosen positions within a sequence directly…">random access</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.suggested: L'accesso casuale, detto anche accesso diretto, è la possibilità di leggere direttamente gli elementi in posizioni scelte di una sequenza, senza doverla scorrere tutta per trovarli (ciò che si chiama accesso sequenziale).
examples.translation: definition prop left verbatim in English; only the label was translated to "accesso casuale"
examples.why: The tooltip text is learner-visible prose, not markup: the link label is Italian but the definition the reader actually opens is still English, so the only explanation of "accesso casuale" is unreadable to an Italian-only learner.

examples.source: ## Query gates
examples.suggested: ## Gate a query
examples.translation: ## gate a query
examples.why: Every other heading in the file is capitalized ("Descrizione del modello", "Esempi di problemi a query"); this one starts lowercase and renders that way in the on-page table of contents.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the two load-bearing passages survive intact: the Sampler/Estimator caveat ("le misurazioni sono obbligatorie … i circuiti inviati a una primitiva Estimator non devono contenere misurazioni") and both `compose`/`decompose` admonitions ("**non** muta nessuno dei circuiti su cui agisce", with `inplace=True` correctly attached). Register is consistently informal-tu (puoi, usa, consulta, tieni presente) and terminology is stable (qubit, gate, circuito, profondità, primitiva, circuiti parametrizzati). Two things a native editor would change: (1) grammatical gender of "gate" is inconsistent inside one sentence — "la [X-gate] è definita come un caso particolare della [U3-gate], un gate a singolo qubit più generale", feminine articles against the masculine "un gate"/"i gate quantistici" used everywhere else; (2) "i cui valori non devono essere specificati fino a poco prima dell'esecuzione" renders the permissive English "do not need to be defined until just before" with "non devono", which reads closer to a prohibition than a deferral — "non è necessario specificarli fino a…" would be unambiguous. Neither misleads about the underlying concept.

examples.source: the [X-gate] is defined as a specific case of the [U3-gate], a more general single-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: il gate X è definito come un caso particolare del gate U3, un gate a singolo qubit più generale.
examples.translation: la [X-gate] è definita come un caso particolare della [U3-gate], un gate a singolo qubit più generale.
examples.why: "gate" is treated as masculine everywhere else in the file ("un gate a singolo qubit", "i gate quantistici" at line 122), but here it takes feminine articles/agreement (la/definita/della) within the very same sentence. A native technical writer would keep one gender.

examples.source: These circuits have undefined parameters, and their values do not need to be defined until just before executing the circuit.
examples.suggested: Questi circuiti hanno parametri non definiti, e non è necessario specificarne i valori fino a poco prima dell'esecuzione del circuito.
examples.translation: Questi circuiti hanno parametri non definiti, i cui valori non devono essere specificati fino a poco prima dell'esecuzione del circuito.
examples.why: English states a permission (you may defer assignment); "non devono essere specificati" leans toward obligation/prohibition. The "fino a" keeps it recoverable, so it does not teach a false rule, but the affordance framing that motivates parameterized circuits is blunted.

editor_note: No misleading content: the crypto substance (RSA key generation, KEM vs. padding-based exchange, DH/DSA, ECDLP, Shor) is faithful, the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("Scegli", "Nota che", "Ricorda", "Puoi provare"), and domain terms are solid and consistent (testo cifrato, testo in chiaro, esponenziazione modulare, totiente, inverso moltiplicativo modulare, crivello del campo numerico generale, fattore primo). What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "computationally infeasible" is rendered four ways — "computazionalmente impossibile" (line 118, a strengthening: infeasible ≠ impossible), "computazionalmente infattibile" (689, 713), "computazionalmente non fattibile" (1499, 1527); likewise "non-repudiation" splits between body "non-repudiabilità" and tooltip "non-ripudio" (the standard Italian term). (2) Two ambiguous/garbled constructions: "un messaggio più lungo di 1024-4096 bit" (line 63) parses as "longer THAN 1024-4096 bits" rather than "a longer, 1024-4096-bit message" (the parallel bullet at line 65 gets it right with parentheses), and "Poiché un KEM puro non richiede padding aggiuntivo, ma…" (line 471) turns the source's "As such" into a causal clause, leaving a "Poiché X, ma Y, Z" sentence whose logic no longer holds together. (3) Scattered calques/typos: "Quasi qualsiasi numero indovineremo andrà bene" (751), "Alice e Bob sono garantiti di ottenere" (915), "nel caso in cui r o s calcolino a 0" (1223), "richiede chiavi di dimensioni comprese tra 2048 bit" (1567), plus "Dato il crescita esponenziale" (713), "decifrandando" (552) and "polologaritimica" (823).

examples.source: Therefore, when using AKC to transmit a symmetric key, for security it must nevertheless be encoded into a longer 1024-4096 bit message.
examples.suggested: …deve comunque essere codificata in un messaggio più lungo, di 1024-4096 bit.
examples.translation: Pertanto, quando si utilizza l'AKC per trasmettere una chiave simmetrica, per sicurezza essa deve comunque essere codificata in un messaggio più lungo di 1024-4096 bit.
examples.why: Without a comma, "più lungo di 1024-4096 bit" reads as "longer THAN 1024-4096 bits", i.e. the message must EXCEED 4096 bits — the opposite of the source, which says the short key is padded up INTO a 1024-4096-bit message. The parallel bullet immediately below (line 65) renders the same quantity correctly as "un messaggio più lungo (1024-4096 bit)", so this is an isolated ambiguity rather than a systematic error.

examples.source: But as shown by Peter Shor in his original 1994 paper, Shor's algorithm also solves the DLP in polynomial-time on quantum computers.
examples.suggested: …l'algoritmo di Shor risolve anche il DLP in tempo polinomiale sui computer quantistici.
examples.translation: Tuttavia, come ha dimostrato Peter Shor nel suo articolo originale del 1994, l'algoritmo di Shor risolve il DLP in tempo polinomiale anche sui computer quantistici.
examples.why: The English "also" scopes over the PROBLEM (in addition to factoring, Shor's algorithm also solves the DLP). The Italian "anche" was moved to scope over the MACHINE, so the sentence reads "solves the DLP in polynomial time on quantum computers TOO" — implying classical computers do it too, which directly contradicts the preceding sentence ("si ritiene che il DLP non abbia una soluzione in tempo polinomiale"). The "Tuttavia" contrast lets a careful reader recover the intent, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: private key secrecy also requires that it be computationally infeasible to derive the private key from knowledge of the public key
examples.suggested: …che sia computazionalmente non fattibile derivare la chiave privata…
examples.translation: la segretezza della chiave privata richiede anche che sia computazionalmente impossibile derivare la chiave privata dalla conoscenza della chiave pubblica
examples.why: "Infeasible" is a hardness claim, not an impossibility claim — "impossibile" strengthens it, which matters pedagogically in a lesson whose whole point is that quantum computers make these problems feasible. The file also uses three different renderings of the same source term: "impossibile" (118), "infattibile" (689, 713), "non fattibile" (1499, 1527).

examples.source: As such a pure KEM does not require additional padding but in this example we are only simulating a KEM using RSA and the `cryptography` library requires the use of padding when encrypting with RSA. So we will use a somewhat shorter long secret…
examples.suggested: Un KEM puro non richiede quindi padding aggiuntivo; in questo esempio, però, stiamo solo simulando un KEM con RSA e la libreria `cryptography` richiede il padding quando si cifra con RSA, per cui useremo un segreto lungo un po' più corto…
examples.translation: Poiché un KEM puro non richiede padding aggiuntivo, ma in questo esempio stiamo solo simulando un KEM usando RSA e la libreria `cryptography` richiede l'uso del padding quando si cifra con RSA, utilizzeremo un lungo segreto leggermente più corto…
examples.why: The source's "As such" (= "therefore") was read as a causal "Poiché", producing an unresolvable "Poiché X, ma Y, Z" period: the stated cause (a pure KEM needs no padding) is not the reason for the conclusion (using a shorter secret) — the real reason sits in the "ma" clause. A native technical writer would break this into two sentences.

examples.source: Almost any number we guess will do the job. / Alice and Bob are guaranteed to end up with the same secret key / requires key sizes in the range of 2048 bits
examples.suggested: Quasi qualsiasi numero scegliamo andrà bene. / È garantito che Alice e Bob ottengano la stessa chiave segreta / richiede chiavi dell'ordine di 2048 bit
examples.translation: Quasi qualsiasi numero indovineremo andrà bene. / Alice e Bob sono garantiti di ottenere la stessa chiave segreta / richiede chiavi di dimensioni comprese tra 2048 bit
examples.why: Three word-for-word calques a native technical editor would rewrite: "numero indovineremo" is ungrammatical (missing relative pronoun, and "indovinare" is the wrong verb for picking a candidate); "X sono garantiti di" is an English passive personal construction Italian does not allow; "comprese tra 2048 bit" opens a range with only one endpoint. None of these changes the meaning, but together with the typos "Dato il crescita" (713), "decifrandando" (552) and "polologaritimica" (823) they leave a machine-translated surface on an otherwise well-rendered lesson.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the PUB structure, the commuting-observables caveat ("Ogni PUB rappresenta una base di misurazione diversa"), all four broadcasting examples with their 5x1/1x1, 5x1/5x1, 1x6/4x1, 3x6/3x1 shapes, and the BitArray axis description ("L'asse più a sinistra ... scorre sugli shot ordinati") all match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register holds ("Se hai...", "esamina", "consulta"). What a native editor would change is the broadcasting-rules block, where the English size/dimension distinction collapses onto one word: "La dimensione di ciascuna dimensione è la dimensione più grande della dimensione corrispondente" (and "Due dimensioni sono compatibili se le loro dimensioni sono uguali") reads as circular and blunts a rule the learner has to act on. Secondly, "bind" is rendered two ways within the same list: "valori parametrici da collegare al circuito" in the Estimator bullet but "devono essere associati a runtime" in the Sampler bullet — "collegare" (connect) is the weaker of the two. Thirdly, "broadcasted shape" becomes "forma trasmessa (broadcasted)" although the file otherwise keeps "broadcasting" in English throughout; "trasmessa" is not the domain sense and only the English gloss rescues it.

examples.source: The size of each dimension is the largest size of the corresponding dimension. ... Two dimensions are compatible if their sizes are equal or if one of them is 1.
examples.suggested: L'ampiezza di ciascuna dimensione è pari alla maggiore fra le ampiezze corrispondenti. ... Due dimensioni sono compatibili se hanno la stessa ampiezza oppure se una delle due vale 1.
examples.translation: La dimensione di ciascuna dimensione è la dimensione più grande della dimensione corrispondente. ... Due dimensioni sono compatibili se le loro dimensioni sono uguali o se una di esse è 1.
examples.why: English distinguishes 'size' from 'dimension'; the Italian uses 'dimensione' for both, producing a circular sentence (four occurrences in one line) that no Italian technical writer would leave. Meaning is recoverable from the examples, so it does not mislead, but the rule stops teaching as clearly as the English.

examples.source: A collection of parameter values to bind the circuit against ... Parameter objects that must be bound at runtime
examples.suggested: Una raccolta di valori dei parametri da associare al circuito ... oggetti `Parameter` che devono essere associati a runtime
examples.translation: Una raccolta di valori parametrici da collegare al circuito ... oggetti `Parameter` che devono essere associati a runtime
examples.why: The same operation ('bind') is rendered 'collegare' in the Estimator bullet and 'associare' four lines later in the Sampler bullet. 'Collegare' means 'connect' and is the weaker rendering; 'associare' is the conventional Italian for parameter binding and should be used in both places.

examples.source: `Estimator` returns one expectation value estimate for each element of the broadcasted shape.
examples.suggested: `Estimator` restituisce una stima del valore di aspettazione per ciascun elemento della forma risultante dal broadcasting.
examples.translation: `Estimator` restituisce una stima del valore di aspettazione per ciascun elemento della forma trasmessa (broadcasted).
examples.why: The file consistently keeps 'broadcasting' in English (heading 'Regole di broadcasting', 'array che fanno broadcasting'), then suddenly translates the participle as 'trasmessa', which in Italian means 'transmitted' and is not the array-shape sense. Only the parenthetical English gloss keeps it identifiable.

editor_note: The math, the proofs in Appendix I/II, and the physics all survive translation intact — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, register is consistently informal "tu" ("Spiega perché", "Sei libero di saltare", "Fai riferimento al grafico"). What a native editor would fix is consistency and a handful of literal word choices: "Hamiltonian" alternates gender across the file ("l'Hamiltoniano"/"gli Hamiltoniani" in §3 and §5 vs "l'Hamiltoniana"/"le nostre Hamiltoniane" in §4), plus an un-elided "sul Hamiltoniano del modello" (~1123); "Krylov method" is "il metodo Krylov" throughout §1 but "il metodo di Krylov" from §2 on, and the lesson's own subject is "diagonalizzazione Krylov quantistica" in the opening line vs "Diagonalizzazione quantistica di Krylov" in the title; "generalized eigenvalue problem" appears as "problema generalizzato agli autovalori", "problema agli autovalori generalizzato" and "problema generalizzato degli autovalori". Literal-but-wrong renderings: "span" becomes the calque "spaziano" ("i vettori che spaziano lo spazio di Krylov", ~400, ~768) where the rest of the file correctly uses "generano"; "scaling" becomes "scalatura/scalature" (~1658-1664) and the §2.2 heading "Time scaling" becomes "Scala temporale" (= "time scale", not "how time scales"); "smooth these curves" becomes "levighiamo queste curve" (~624, ~676); "vacuum state" becomes "stato vuoto" instead of "stato di vuoto" (~1128); "orthogonalization" is rendered "ortonormalizzazione" in four places (incl. FOM = "metodo di ortonormalizzazione completa") but "ortogonalizzazione" at ~693. One referent drift at ~196 and a plain typo "richediamo" (~687) round it out; none of these would teach a learner a false concept.

examples.source: Indeed, as we will see in later sections, the Krylov method is only advantageous above a certain matrix dimension; this is intended to help us solve eigenvalue/eigenvector problems of extremely large matrices.
examples.suggested: ...; il metodo è inteso ad aiutarci a risolvere problemi di autovalori/autovettori di matrici estremamente grandi.
examples.translation: Infatti, come vedremo nelle sezioni successive, il metodo Krylov è vantaggioso solo al di sopra di una certa dimensione della matrice; questo esempio è inteso ad aiutarci a risolvere problemi di autovalori/autovettori di matrici estremamente grandi.
examples.why: EN's 'this' refers to the Krylov METHOD; the translation pins it on 'questo esempio' — the 3x3 toy matrix — which flatly contradicts the preceding sentence ('In questo esempio, il metodo Krylov potrebbe non sembrare particolarmente più semplice'). Confusing rather than concept-breaking, but a wrong referent the editor must fix.

examples.source: the Hamiltonian / a Hamiltonian / Hamiltonians
examples.suggested: Pick one gender throughout — conventional Italian physics usage is feminine: «l'hamiltoniana», «le hamiltoniane», «l'hamiltoniana proiettata».
examples.translation: «il numero di termini di Pauli non commutanti che compongono l'Hamiltoniano» (695) vs «calcola l'energia dello stato fondamentale di un'Hamiltoniana, usando l'Hamiltoniana e il numero di qubit» (847) vs «gli Hamiltoniani hanno in generale termini che non possono essere misurati simultaneamente» (1662) vs «proiettare le nostre Hamiltoniane su sottospazi più grandi» (971)
examples.why: The gender flips by section (masculine in §3 and §5, feminine in §4), so the same object is called both 'l'Hamiltoniano' and 'l'Hamiltoniana' within one lesson. Concept stays identifiable, so MINOR — but it reads as two translators merged.

examples.source: the generation of the vectors spanning the Krylov space ... The coefficients in c determine the contribution of the different vectors that span K_U.
examples.suggested: i vettori che generano lo spazio di Krylov ... i diversi vettori che generano $\mathcal{K}_U$
examples.translation: la generazione dei vettori che spaziano lo spazio di Krylov ... i diversi vettori che spaziano $\mathcal{K}_U$
examples.why: 'spaziare' in Italian means to range/roam, not to span a vector space; the correct verb is 'generare' (or 'sottendere'), which this very file uses everywhere else ('lo spazio generato dai vettori', ~30; 'vettori che generano l'intero spazio', ~104). A pure calque on English 'span'.

examples.source: This table collects some scaling of different steps for consideration. / A table describing scaling of different processes ... / 2.2 Time scaling with matrix dimension
examples.suggested: «...raccoglie gli andamenti di scala dei diversi passaggi»; «che descrive come scalano i diversi processi»; heading: «Andamento del tempo di calcolo con la dimensione della matrice» (or «Scalabilità temporale...»).
examples.translation: Questa tabella raccoglie alcune scalature di diversi passaggi a titolo di confronto. / Una tabella che descrive la scalatura di diversi processi ... / 2.2 Scala temporale con la dimensione della matrice
examples.why: 'scalatura' means climbing/scaling a wall, not asymptotic scaling; and 'Scala temporale' reads as 'time scale' rather than 'how the time scales with dimension' — which is exactly what §2.2 measures. Recognizable from context, hence MINOR, but not what a quantum engineer would write.

examples.source: there are many cases where it is safe to assume that there is a vacuum state (in this case it maps to the |0>^N state) which is unaffected by the action of the Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: ...è lecito assumere la presenza di uno stato di vuoto...
examples.translation: esistono molti casi in cui è lecito assumere la presenza di uno stato vuoto (in questo caso corrispondente allo stato $|0\rangle^N$) che non è influenzato dall'azione dell'Hamiltoniano
examples.why: In Italian physics the vacuum state is 'lo stato di vuoto'; 'uno stato vuoto' reads as 'an empty state', a different (and meaningless) notion here. Imperfect but recognizable from the |0>^N gloss that follows.

examples.source: Using the unitary Krylov subspace can be shown to give similar convergence guarantees as the power Krylov subspace
examples.suggested: Si può dimostrare che l'uso del sottospazio di Krylov unitario fornisce garanzie di convergenza simili a quelle del sottospazio di Krylov delle potenze
examples.translation: L'uso del sottospazio di Krylov unitario può essere dimostrato fornire garanzie di convergenza simili a quelle del sottospazio di Krylov potenza
examples.why: 'può essere dimostrato fornire' is a raw calque of the English raising construction 'can be shown to give' and is not grammatical Italian; the language requires 'si può dimostrare che ... fornisce'. Stiffness only — the claim itself is faithful.

examples.source: Some important factors are the precision we require and the sparsity of the matrices being diagonalized.
examples.suggested: ...la precisione che richiediamo...
examples.translation: Alcuni fattori importanti sono la precisione che richediamo e la sparsità delle matrici da diagonalizzare.
examples.why: Plain typo ('richediamo' → 'richiediamo') inside an answer accordion a learner will read.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every instruction, caveat and version constraint (qiskit>=0.45,<1, 1.0.0rc1, the "do NOT build the environment with several pip install commands" warning, the "this process deliberately creates an invalid environment" admonition) is carried over faithfully, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is a handful of calques plus one ungrammatical form: "the dependent (package)" is rendered as the bare noun "Il dipendente", which in Italian first reads as "the employee" and should be "il pacchetto dipendente" (recurs three times); "It's not possible to backdate requirements changes" becomes "Non è possibile retrodate le modifiche ai requisiti", where "retrodate" is not a valid infinitive ("retrodatare"); "the long-obsolete Qiskit IBM Q Provider" is calqued as "il lungo-obsoleto ... Provider". There is also a subject-verb agreement slip in "Le regole predefinite di Python cercano ... quando tenta di importare un modulo" (needs "si tenta"/"tentano"), and "branch-protecting on CI success against the Qiskit main branch" is calqued as "in base al successo della CI contro il branch main" while the immediately preceding sentence correctly writes "ai test proattivi sul branch main". None of these would lead a learner to do the wrong thing.

examples.source: The dependent is an old package, and will not be updated to support Qiskit v1.0.
examples.suggested: Il pacchetto dipendente è vecchio e non verrà aggiornato per supportare Qiskit v1.0.
examples.translation: Il dipendente è un pacchetto vecchio, e non verrà aggiornato per supportare Qiskit v1.0.
examples.why: 'Il dipendente' as a standalone noun reads in Italian as 'the employee'; the technical sense needs the head noun 'pacchetto'. Recoverable from context (the sentence itself says 'è un pacchetto'), so MINOR, but it recurs in the second bullet ('Il dipendente è un pacchetto attivamente mantenuto') and in 'caratterizzato dal dipendente che si trova all'ultima versione'.

examples.source: It's not possible to backdate requirements changes to previously released versions
examples.suggested: Non è possibile retrodatare le modifiche ai requisiti alle versioni già rilasciate
examples.translation: Non è possibile retrodate le modifiche ai requisiti alle versioni già rilasciate
examples.why: 'retrodate' is not a valid Italian infinitive; after 'Non è possibile' the verb must be 'retrodatare'. A plain grammatical slip no native writer would produce.

examples.source: the long-obsolete Qiskit IBM Q Provider
examples.suggested: il da tempo obsoleto Qiskit IBM Q Provider
examples.translation: il lungo-obsoleto Qiskit IBM Q Provider
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English compound adjective; 'lungo-obsoleto' is not Italian and marks the sentence as machine-translated.

examples.source: Python's default rules search the current working directory very early in the search path when trying to `import` a module
examples.suggested: ... molto presto nel percorso di ricerca quando si tenta di importare un modulo
examples.translation: Le regole predefinite di Python cercano la directory di lavoro corrente molto presto nel percorso di ricerca quando tenta di importare un modulo
examples.why: Subject-verb agreement breaks: the subject is plural ('Le regole ... cercano') but the subordinate verb is singular ('tenta'). Needs 'tentano' or an impersonal 'si tenta'.

examples.source: We do not recommend initially branch-protecting on CI success against the Qiskit `main` branch
examples.suggested: ... in base al successo della CI sul branch `main` di Qiskit
examples.translation: Non ti consigliamo inizialmente di proteggere i branch in base al successo della CI contro il branch `main` di Qiskit
examples.why: 'contro il branch' calques English 'against'; Italian uses 'sul/con'. The preceding sentence already gets it right ('ai test proattivi sul branch `main`'), so the file is internally inconsistent, and 'contro l'ultima release candidate' repeats the calque.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the pedagogy holds (primale/duale, kernel trick, percettrone, data reuploading, informal "tu" used consistently: "il tuo dataset", "Ricorda che...", "Potresti iniziare la tua rete neurale"). The one real semantic slip is in "Passare a spazi di dimensione superiore": EN "not sufficient for improvement over classical methods" became "non sono sufficienti per migliorare i metodi classici", i.e. "to improve the classical methods" instead of "for an improvement over/rispetto ai metodi classici" — the insufficiency claim survives, so it is imprecise rather than misleading. The rest is calqued phrasing a native technical editor would rewrite: "molto alta-dimensionale" / "infinite-dimensionali" (Italian: "ad alta dimensionalità" / "a dimensione infinita", and the file itself elsewhere uses "a dimensione inferiore" vs "a bassa dimensione"), "in alcuni sensi il modo più diretto" for "in some ways", the recurring "vettori mappati dalle feature" for "feature-mapped vectors" (literally "mapped by the features"), "la traccia di qubit fuori dal circuito" for "tracing qubits out" (should be traccia parziale / "tracing out"), plus one agreement error, "potrebbe esserci pesi non nulli" → "potrebbero esserci".

examples.source: The dimensionality of data features is important, but high-dimensional quantum states are not sufficient for improvement over classical methods.
examples.suggested: ...non sono sufficienti per ottenere un miglioramento rispetto ai metodi classici.
examples.translation: La dimensionalità delle feature dei dati è importante, ma gli stati quantistici ad alta dimensionalità non sono sufficienti per migliorare i metodi classici.
examples.why: "per migliorare i metodi classici" reads as improving the classical methods themselves; the English says high-dimensional quantum states alone do not buy you an advantage OVER classical methods. Direction of the claim is preserved, so imprecise rather than misleading.

examples.source: Generally, there could be non-zero weights between all neurons of all layers
examples.suggested: In generale, potrebbero esserci pesi non nulli tra tutti i neuroni di tutti gli strati
examples.translation: In generale, potrebbe esserci pesi non nulli tra tutti i neuroni di tutti gli strati
examples.why: Number agreement error: plural subject "pesi" requires "potrebbero esserci".

examples.suggested: ...e il tracciamento parziale (tracing out) dei qubit fuori dal circuito.
examples.translation: ...misurazioni a metà circuito o circuiti dinamici, e la traccia di qubit fuori dal circuito.
examples.why: "tracing out" is the partial-trace operation; "la traccia di qubit fuori dal circuito" is a literal rendering that does not name the operation an Italian reader would recognize (traccia parziale).

examples.suggested: prodotti interni tra i vettori trasformati dalla mappa delle feature per input diversi
examples.translation: prodotti interni tra vettori mappati dalle feature di input diversi
examples.why: "mappati dalle feature" literally says "mapped by the features"; the vectors are mapped BY the feature map. Used consistently, so recognizable, but it is an imperfect rendering repeated across the kernel section.

examples.source: in some ways the most straightforward way is that shown in $f_1$ below
examples.suggested: per certi versi il modo più diretto è quello mostrato in $f_1$ qui sotto
examples.translation: in alcuni sensi il modo più diretto è quello mostrato in $f_1$ qui sotto
examples.why: "in alcuni sensi" is a word-for-word calque of "in some ways"; Italian technical prose uses "per certi versi" / "in un certo senso".

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every card description maps faithfully onto its English counterpart (e.g. circuit cutting "隣接しないQubit間のエンタングリングゲートを分解することで、トランスパイル済みCircuitの深度を削減します", SLC's PEC-overhead sentence, and the M3 "ノイズのあるビット列で定義された縮小部分空間" line are all accurate). What a native technical editor would change: (1) "observable" is split within the file — オブザーバブル in the OBP card and the "期待値推定におけるノイズ管理" intro, but 観測量 in the PNA and Shaded-lightcones cards right below it; (2) "circuit depth" is likewise split between 回路深度 (AQC-Tensor card) and Circuit深度 (section heading and OBP card); (3) the PNA card's "期待値を軽減します" reads as "lower the expectation values" rather than "mitigate error in the expectation values" — recognizable from context but the wrong verb-object pairing for 誤差緩和; (4) two ご利用ください instances (lines 71 and 132) are the honorific register the house style excludes. None of these would teach a false concept.

examples.source: Reduce circuit depth in expectation value estimations by backpropagating observables through the circuit. / …measuring a target observable that has absorbed noise model information.
examples.suggested: Use オブザーバブル throughout (or 観測量 throughout) — pick one and apply it in all four places, including 「観測量推定への影響が低い」→「オブザーバブル推定への影響が低い」.
examples.translation: Circuit全体にオブザーバブルをバックプロパゲートすることで… / ノイズモデル情報を吸収したターゲット観測量を測定することで…
examples.why: ‘Observable’ is rendered two ways within the same page, and the two spellings sit in adjacent cards under the same heading, so a learner may not realize they denote the same object.

examples.source: Construct high-fidelity circuits with reduced depth… / These capabilities are useful for reducing circuit depth…
examples.suggested: Make the compound consistent with the file's kept-English convention: 「Circuit深度を削減しながら高忠実度のCircuitを構築します」.
examples.translation: 回路深度を削減しながら高忠実度のCircuitを構築します。 / これらの機能はCircuit深度の削減に有効であり…
examples.why: The same compound noun 'circuit depth' appears as both 回路深度 and Circuit深度, and the AQC-Tensor card even mixes 回路深度 with Circuit in one sentence.

examples.source: Mitigate expectation values by measuring a target observable that has absorbed noise model information.
examples.suggested: …を測定することで、期待値の誤差を緩和します。
examples.translation: ノイズモデル情報を吸収したターゲット観測量を測定することで、期待値を軽減します。
examples.why: 軽減 taking 期待値 as its direct object reads as 'reduce the expectation value' in Japanese; the intended sense is error mitigation applied to the estimate, which 期待値の誤差を緩和 states unambiguously. 軽減 is correct in the other cards where the object is 測定エラー.

examples.source: Use the following addons to manage noise… / Use these capabilities to support and compose your workflows…
examples.suggested: …以下のアドオンを使用します。 / …これらの機能を使用します。
examples.translation: …ノイズ管理には、以下のアドオンをご利用ください。 / …これらの機能をご利用ください。
examples.why: ご利用ください is the honorific register the file's house style excludes; plain desu/masu is used everywhere else on the page, so these two lines stand out.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the whole Pauli-decomposition / syndrome-collapse / product-state argument (積状態, 密度行列 $\xi$, エントロピー) tracks the English step for step, and domain terms are right (シンドローム, パウリ行列, クラウス表現, 脱分極チャネル, 部分空間). Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) L34 has a genuine garden-path word order, 「どの量子ビットにある量子ビットユニタリ演算が作用するか」, which first parses as "the ... that is on which qubit" instead of "which qubit a given unitary acts on"; (2) "encoding / encoded state" is rendered two ways in the same file — 符号化 (L51, L84, L104, L114) vs エンコードされた状態 (L30, L32, L169) — a consistency slip, not a comprehension problem; (3) L112 「良すぎる話に思える」 is a calque of "too good to be true" (native register would be うますぎる話 / 出来すぎた話), and in the same sentence English's concessive "even errors that are tiny" is folded into a plain modifier, so the emphasis that *even* imperceptible errors are covered is flattened. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: it will be convenient to use subscripts to indicate which qubit a given qubit unitary operation acts upon.
examples.suggested: ある量子ビットユニタリ演算がどの量子ビットに作用するかを示す添字を用いると便利です。
examples.translation: どの量子ビットにある量子ビットユニタリ演算が作用するかを示す添字を用いると便利です。
examples.why: 「どの量子ビットにある」 reads at first pass as "which qubit's ...", forcing a re-read. Fronting the subject restores the natural Japanese order and removes the garden path; no meaning change.

examples.source: the state of the encoding / the original encoded state / the 9-qubit encoding of a qubit state
examples.suggested: 符号化(された状態) に統一
examples.translation: エンコードされた状態 (L30, L32, L169) と 符号化 (L51, L84, L104, L114) が併存
examples.why: Same concept rendered two ways inside one short lesson. The concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a comprehension defect, but an editor would unify on 符号化.

examples.source: At first glance it may seem too good to be true that we can correct for arbitrary unitary errors like this, even errors that are tiny and hardly noticeable on their own.
examples.suggested: 一見すると、任意のユニタリ誤りを、しかもそれ単体ではほとんど気づかないほど微小な誤りまで、このように訂正できるというのはうますぎる話に思えるかもしれません。
examples.translation: 一見すると、非常に小さくてそれ単体ではほとんど気づかないような任意のユニタリ誤りをこのように訂正できるのは、良すぎる話に思えるかもしれません。
examples.why: 「良すぎる話」 is a word-for-word calque of "too good to be true"; うますぎる話/出来すぎた話 is what a Japanese technical writer would write. Also English's "even errors that are tiny" is concessive — the surprise is that *even* imperceptible errors are covered — whereas the translation turns it into a plain attributive, flattening the emphasis.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the blocking-call caveat for job.result() ("ジョブが完了するまでブロッキング呼び出しとなります"), the "retired QPUs" parenthetical in the service.jobs() paragraph, and the deprecated-provider Admonition (qiskit-ibm-provider jobs still returned vs qiskit-ibmq-provider jobs "もはや利用できません") all match the English exactly, and job/workload/backend/Sampler terminology is consistent. Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) In the Analytics paragraph, "ご自身が所有または管理しているアカウントのみ表示可能です" drops the required scoping particle — it should be "…アカウントでのみ閲覧できます"; as written it parses as "only accounts … are displayable", and the source's "Note that" hedge is dropped with no ご注意ください equivalent. (2) Mild honorific slips against the plain desu/masu convention: "ご自身" (L25) and "お試しください" (L152) — neither misleads, but both are the keigo register the house style avoids.

examples.source: Note that you can only see the Analytics page for accounts that you own or manage.
examples.suggested: なお、アナリティクスページは、自分が所有または管理しているアカウントでのみ閲覧できます。
examples.translation: アナリティクスページは、ご自身が所有または管理しているアカウントのみ表示可能です。
examples.why: Missing the scoping particle で before のみ — "アカウントのみ表示可能" reads as "only accounts are displayable" rather than "viewable only for accounts you own/manage". The English hedge "Note that" is also dropped with no なお/ご注意 equivalent.

examples.source: Try the Grover's algorithm tutorial.
examples.suggested: …チュートリアルを試してみてください。
examples.translation: [グローバーのアルゴリズム](/tutorials/grovers-algorithm)チュートリアルをお試しください。
examples.why: お試しください is the honorific o-…-kudasai pattern the file's plain desu/masu convention avoids; same slip class as ご自身 on line 25. Not misleading, purely register.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — the load-bearing claims all survive intact (the bolded 「エンタングルした量子状態の高次元性は指数的な並列性ではなく…十分条件でもありません」, the dequantization definition 「多項式的にしか遅くない」, the Liu/Arunachalam/Temme discrete-log quote, and the diagonal-entry answer 「対角エントリは 1.0」 are all correct), so nothing here would teach a false concept. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "Managing expectations" is rendered 「期待値の管理」 — a defensible business idiom, but in a quantum document 期待値 is the reserved term for *expectation value*, and it also leaks into the frontmatter description 「期待値の設定」; 期待の管理 / 現実的な期待 avoids the collision. (2) "qubit" is split within the file between 量子ビット (lines ~34, ~75) and キュービット (lines ~61, ~75 — both forms appear in the same paragraph), and "utility scale" is split between 実用スケール (~48) and ユーティリティスケール (~165). (3) Two translationese slips: "statement" is consistently rendered 「発言」 (an utterance/remark) where 記述/主張 is meant, and "near-term quantum computers" becomes 「近期の量子コンピュータ」, a Sinitic form Japanese technical prose does not use (近い将来の / 短期的な). (4) One sentence is present in the translation but absent from the English source — 「以下の質問を読んで、答えを考えてから、三角形をクリックして解答を表示してください。」 before the check-your-understanding block — plus two dropped hedges (perhaps/might) in the supervised/unsupervised figure caption. None of these mislead; register is correct desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: ## Managing expectations
examples.suggested: ## 期待の管理  (frontmatter: 現実的な期待の提示)
examples.translation: ## 期待値の管理
examples.why: 期待値 is the standard Japanese rendering of *expectation value*, a core term in this very course (Estimator/期待値). Using it for 'expectations' in a quantum-ML document creates an avoidable domain collision; context disambiguates, so it is imperfect-but-recognizable rather than misleading.

examples.source: qubits / a qubit
examples.suggested: 量子ビット throughout
examples.translation: 量子ビット (l.34, l.75) vs キュービット (l.61, l.75)
examples.why: Both renderings appear, twice within the same paragraph at ~l.75 (「量子ビットが複数の状態に…」 then 「…重ね合わせ状態にキュービットを準備できますが」). Same issue for utility scale: 実用スケール (l.48) vs ユーティリティスケール (l.165).

examples.source: This is a true statement, but it is inadequate… / The above statements have been made very carefully…
examples.suggested: これは正しい記述ですが… / 上記の記述は非常に慎重に述べられており…
examples.translation: これは真の発言ですが… / 上記の発言は非常に慎重に述べられており…
examples.why: 発言 means an utterance/remark by a speaker; for a written mathematical/expository claim a Japanese technical writer would use 記述 or 主張. Reads as a dictionary-first rendering of 'statement'. Similarly 「近期の量子コンピュータ」 (l.55) for 'near-term quantum computers' — 近期 is not idiomatic Japanese; use 近い将来の or 短期的な.

examples.source: (no corresponding sentence in the English source — EN goes straight from the '### Check your understanding' heading to the question)
examples.suggested: delete the sentence
examples.translation: 以下の質問を読んで、答えを考えてから、三角形をクリックして解答を表示してください。
examples.why: An instruction present in the translation but not in the source. It is benign UI guidance that happens to match the rendered <details> disclosure, so it does not mislead about the subject matter, but it is added prose. In the same region, two hedges are dropped in the figure caption (~l.41): 'perhaps looking for clusters' → 「クラスターを探索します」 and 'clusters the algorithm might identify' → 「アルゴリズムが識別するクラスター」, both stating as certain what the English leaves tentative.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, no hallucination; core terms (トランスパイル / トランスパイラーパス / パスマネージャー / ステージ付きパスマネージャー / 基底ゲートセット / モック・バックエンド) are correct and consistent, and register is plain です・ます with no keigo. Two naturalness-only nits: (1) the "useful abstraction" sentence in the staged-pass-manager paragraph is packed into one long center-embedded sentence (「これはトランスパイルが通常、…各ステージがパスマネージャーで表される離散的なステージで行われるため、有用な抽象化です。」) that a native technical writer would split in two, since the reason clause and the nested relative clause on 「ステージ」 collide; (2) 「回路にパスマネージャーを実行するには」 takes the wrong particle for 実行する with a pass manager as object — 「回路に対してパスマネージャーを実行するには」, the phrasing the same file already uses earlier (「回路に対してそれらを実行できるオブジェクト」). Neither would mislead a learner; content-wise this is a clean translation.

examples.source: This is a useful abstraction because transpilation typically happens in discrete stages, as described in Transpiler stages, with each stage being represented by a pass manager.
examples.suggested: トランスパイルは通常、[トランスパイラーのステージ](transpiler-stages)で説明されているように、離散的なステージに分かれて行われ、各ステージがパスマネージャーで表されます。そのため、これは有用な抽象化です。
examples.translation: これはトランスパイルが通常、[トランスパイラーのステージ](transpiler-stages)で説明されているように、各ステージがパスマネージャーで表される離散的なステージで行われるため、有用な抽象化です。
examples.why: The English is one clause with a trailing 'with...' adjunct; the Japanese folds all of it into a single because-clause with 「各ステージがパスマネージャーで表される」 embedded as a relative clause on 「ステージ」, so the reader hits 「ステージ」 twice in different roles before reaching the predicate 「有用な抽象化です」. Grammatical and accurate, but it reads as calqued English syntax rather than something a Japanese quantum engineer would write; splitting into two sentences restores the English's pacing.

examples.source: To run the pass manager on the circuit, call the `run` method.
examples.suggested: 回路に対してパスマネージャーを実行するには、`run` メソッドを呼び出します。
examples.translation: 回路にパスマネージャーを実行するには、`run` メソッドを呼び出します。
examples.why: 「回路に…を実行する」 is an unidiomatic particle choice — 実行する does not take a に-marked target this way; the natural rendering of 'run X on Y' here is 「Yに対してXを実行する」. The file itself already uses the correct form earlier (「回路に対してそれらを実行できるオブジェクトです」), so this is also an internal inconsistency in phrasing.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — the coin-flip enumeration, the $2^n$ cost-minimization example, the "only one result is measured" caveat, the scarf entanglement metaphor with its "this metaphor is imperfect" qualifier, and all three quiz answers (誤りです／正しいです／上記すべて) match the English exactly, and core terms (量子ビット, 重ね合わせ, エンタングルメント, 干渉, 量子回路) are correct and consistent. Six editorial slips, none misleading: (1) "classical probabilism" is rendered 古典的な確率論 ("probability theory", the mathematical field) in both the body and the final takeaway, where 古典的な確率性／確率的混合 is meant; (2) the Darío Gil video intro drops the English hedge "may be beyond the reach" → 「世界最大のスーパーコンピューターでも手の届かないビジネス上の問題」, asserting flatly what the source hedges; (3) the first quiz answer adds a contrast clause not in the source (「難しさは複雑な数式ではなく、直感に反する性質にあります」 vs. plain "Their difficulty lies in their counterintuitive nature") plus an unsourced intensifier はるかに; (4) two humble/polite-form register slips against the desu/masu-no-keigo convention — 「全体を見ていただいても構いません」 and 「以下の動画でご確認ください」; (5) 参照してください is used as the catch-all for "watch this video", producing the stiff 「…比較と、…価値を参照してください」; (6) Katie Pizzolato's title is compressed to 「IBM Quantumの副社長」, dropping "Platform" and using 副社長 (deputy-president rank) for a US-corporate VP.

examples.source: quantum superposition is more powerful than classical probabilism
examples.suggested: 量子の重ね合わせは古典的な確率性（確率的な混合）よりも強力です
examples.translation: 量子の重ね合わせは古典的な確率論よりも強力です
examples.why: 確率論 names the mathematical discipline of probability theory, not the classical probabilistic behavior being contrasted. Recognizable in context, so MINOR, but it makes the sentence read as "superposition beats probability theory", which is a category error. Occurs identically in the Key takeaways bullet.

examples.source: quantum algorithms can be developed that can solve business problems that may be beyond the reach of even the world's largest supercomputers
examples.suggested: 世界最大のスーパーコンピューターでも手が届かないかもしれないビジネス上の問題を解決しうる量子アルゴリズムを開発できます
examples.translation: 世界最大のスーパーコンピューターでも手の届かないビジネス上の問題を解決する量子アルゴリズムを開発できます
examples.why: The English double-hedges ("may be beyond the reach", "can solve"); the Japanese states it as established fact. A dropped qualifier that strengthens a forward-looking claim — MINOR per the rubric, but worth restoring in course material aimed at business decision-makers.

examples.source: False. Being only a little more complex than high school algebra, quantum concepts are more accessible that one might think. Their difficulty lies in their counterintuitive nature.
examples.suggested: 誤りです。量子の概念は高校代数より少し複雑な程度であり、思われているよりも身近なものです。難しさは、直感に反する性質にあります。
examples.translation: 誤りです。量子の概念は高校代数より少し複雑な程度であり、思われているよりもはるかに身近なものです。難しさは複雑な数式ではなく、直感に反する性質にあります。
examples.why: Adds a contrastive clause (「複雑な数式ではなく」) and an intensifier (はるかに) that are not in the source. The addition happens to agree with the surrounding section, so it does not mislead, but it is invented text in a graded-answer block where fidelity matters most.

examples.source: feel free to watch the entire video / Learn how to pronounce this word and more in the video below.
examples.suggested: 全体を見ても構いません／以下の動画で確認してください
examples.translation: 全体を見ていただいても構いません／以下の動画でご確認ください
examples.why: いただく and ご+確認+ください are humble/honorific forms the file's convention (plain desu/masu, no keigo) excludes; the rest of the file stays correctly in ~してください／~ます. Two isolated slips, so MINOR.

examples.source: Watch the video below to see how classical and quantum circuits compare and how quantum circuits can bring value to your business.
examples.suggested: 以下の動画では、古典的な回路と量子回路の比較、そして量子回路がビジネスにもたらす価値を紹介します。
examples.translation: 以下の動画で、古典的回路と量子回路の比較と、量子回路があなたのビジネスにもたらす価値を参照してください。
examples.why: 参照してください is being used as a blanket stand-in for "watch" throughout the file; taking 比較 and 価値 as its objects is a calque no Japanese technical writer would produce (one "refers to" a document, not to a comparison shown in a video). Also あなたのビジネス is a literal carry-over of possessive "your".

examples.why: 副社長 denotes deputy-president rank in a Japanese company, well above a US-corporate VP; the standard rendering is バイスプレジデント or ~担当副社長. The "IBM Quantum Platform" portfolio is also dropped from the title.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — no drift, no hallucination. The one passage that could mislead if inverted, the removal note (L35), keeps the direction correct: そのユーザーのワークロードおよび関連する結果はそのユーザーには表示されなくなります / 同じインスタンス内の他のユーザーは引き続き…アクセスできます. Terminology is correct and consistent (アクセスグループ, インスタンス, オーバーフローメニュー, ワークロード, アカウント切り替え used identically in both occurrences). Two cosmetic points a Japanese technical editor would still change: in the "推奨事項" list the third bullet puts the sentence-final 。 *inside* the link text (「[アクセスグループを作成および管理します。](/guides/access-groups)」), so the period is rendered as part of the hyperlink, unlike the two bullets above it where the 。 sits outside the link; and the same list renders EN's imperative recommendations as flat declaratives 「…を作成します / …を理解します」, which reads as a description of what happens rather than as advice.
